players.product: thermal processing equipment for AI advanced packaging and AI server board assembly (Thermal Processing Solutions segment)

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal 2025 (year ended September 30, 2025) by segment, in thousands: net revenue - Thermal Processing Solutions (TPS) $58,057 (-16%), Semiconductor Fabrication Solutions (SFS) $21,307 (-34%), total $79,364 (-22%); TPS was 73% of consolidated net revenue. New orders - TPS $51,867 (+5%), SFS $22,074 (-26%), total $73,941 (-7%). Backlog at September 30, 2025 - TPS $14,655 (-30%), SFS $5,234 (+17%), total $19,889 (-21%). Gross margin: TPS stayed at 35% in 2025 and 2024 - the filing cites inventory obsolescence expense and unfavorable product mix (fewer shipments of lower-margin high-temperature furnaces and BDF equipment), partly offset by the employee retention credit, and an increase in shipments of its higher-margin advanced packaging SPG equipment; SFS fell to 30% from 37% due primarily to inventory obsolescence caused by a decline in the mature node semiconductor market.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 revenue $79,364 thousand (-22%); TPS $58,057 thousand (-16%); new orders $73,941 thousand (-7%); backlog $19,889 thousand (-21%)

quarterly_data.signal: Manufacturing and supply (10-K): reflow equipment and furnaces are manufactured at Amtech's ISO 9001:2015 certified facility in Shanghai, China and by contract manufacturing partners in China, Canada and Singapore. Flip-chip reflow systems (rated up to 400 C) are built in Shanghai and by a contract manufacturer in Singapore, which the filing says will build Pyramax furnaces for North American and European customers; high-temperature belt furnaces (up to 1180 C) are built in Shanghai and by a contract manufacturer in Canada - partnering with that CM since 2023 produced record belt-furnace shipments. Key vendors include suppliers of controllers, quartz and silicon carbide for diffusion systems, specialized steel mills in Germany and Japan, an injection molding machine, an adhesive manufacturer and a single-sourced pad supplier from Japan; some key parts come from a single or limited number of suppliers. Fiscal 2025 capital expenditures were $1.0 million, and management expects capital expenditures to decrease slightly in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: contract manufacturers in Canada and Singapore; FY2025 capex $1.0 million
